title: Cited but Unused: Parametric Provenance in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: arXiv:2611.17161v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation systems attach citations to attribute claims to their sources. These citations frequently misstate provenance, and standard verification cannot detect this. We measure provenance by counterfactual value substitution: a fact in the retrieved passages is replaced with a false variant and the model re-queried. We find that across five sizes of one model family and a second comparator family, 1.2% to 15.7% of citable claims derive from parametric memory rather than the retrieved context. At the most conservative substitution distance these figures are 4.6% and 8.5% on the two models we tested at it, with the rate rising with model size within a family. We further find that natural language inference verification, the standard approach, gives results indistinguishable from chance across models, even when restricted to the cited passage. We determine that the cause is structural: a model answering from memory sel

translated_title: 被引用却未被使用：检索增强生成中的参数记忆来源问题
translated_abstract: 检索增强生成系统通过附加引用将声明归属于其来源。这些引用经常错误地陈述真实来源，而标准验证方法无法检测到这一点。我们通过反事实值替换来衡量来源：将检索段落中的某个事实替换为虚假变体，然后重新查询模型。我们发现，在一个模型家族的五个不同规模以及另一个对比模型家族中，1.2%到15.7%的可引用声明实际上源自参数记忆而非检索到的上下文。在最保守的替换距离下，我们测试的两个模型上这一比例分别为4.6%和8.5%，且该比例在家族内随模型规模增大而上升。我们进一步发现，作为标准方法的自然语言推理验证，在各模型上给出的结果与随机猜测无异，即使仅限于被引用的段落也是如此。我们确定原因是结构性的：从记忆中作答的模型……
tldr: 该论文提出用反事实值替换法来衡量检索增强生成的真实来源，发现1.2%至15.7%的可引用声明实际来自模型的参数记忆而非检索内容，且标准的自然语言推理验证对此完全失效，其表现与随机猜测无异。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces counterfactual value substitution to measure true provenance in retrieval-augmented generation, finding that 1.2%–15.7% of citable claims actually derive from parametric memory rather than the retrieved context, while standard natural language inference verification performs no better than chance.
